instruction: Open the link embedded in the latest Bills folder email in a new tab in Chrome.

metadata.explanation: Variation 3: Emphasizing 'embedded link' and 'new tab'. Task asks to open the first hyperlink from the latest Bills email as a new Chrome tab. Evaluator checks that the amazon.com URL is added to the existing tabs.

llm_judge_reasons: Semantic mismatch: Evaluator uses exact list matching for all tabs, but instruction only requires adding ONE new tab (amazon.com). This is overly strict.
Fragile verification: Will fail if initial tabs are closed, reordered, or if extra tabs exist - even though the core requirement (opening amazon.com in new tab) was completed.
The metric is_expected_tabs uses are_lists_equal which requires exact tab list match [apple.com, scholar.google.com, amazon.com], not just checking if amazon.com was added.
Expected value (amazon.com) appears correct based on metadata explanation, but cannot be independently verified from task JSON.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Use a metric that checks 'amazon.com tab is present among open tabs' rather than requiring exact list matching of all tabs.
Consider subset-based verification: Check that amazon.com is in the tab list, optionally verify initial tabs (apple.com, scholar.google.com) are still present.
Alternative: Check tab count is 3 (initial 2 + new 1) AND amazon.com is one of them, allowing for tab order flexibility.
Clarify task requirement: Does the task require initial tabs to remain open, or only that amazon.com is opened in a new tab?
